items.definition:
to tempt
He tried to seduce her with promises of wealth.

to avoid
After the scandal, he was shunned by his former friends.

to distort, to bias
The results were skewed by the small sample size.

to combine, to create
Scientists can synthesize new materials in the lab.

to perceive or recognize something
It was difficult to discern the truth from the rumors.

to take part in; to eat or drink
Guests were invited to partake in the feast.

to make worse
The lack of rain will only exacerbate the drought.

send (a prisoner or accused person) back into custody, especially to await trial or further examination
The judge decided to remand the suspect in custody.

to make insane; to disturb the order of
The stress of the situation seemed to derange his thoughts.

to make someone very weak and infirm
The illness can severely debilitate patients.

drive out or expel (someone) from a position or place
The rebels tried to oust the dictator from power.

make (something) continue indefinitely
The cycle of poverty is perpetuated by lack of education.

formally declare one's abandonment of (a claim, right, or possession)
He decided to renounce his claim to the throne.

to attempt to persuade people of the merits of
The company continued to tout its new product as revolutionary.

To free from illusion; to disappoint
The harsh reality began to disillusion him.

to accept and allow (behavior that is considered morally wrong or offensive) to continue
The school does not condone bullying of any kind.

to make or declare (something, typically a church) sacred; dedicate formally to a religious or divine purpose
The bishop will consecrate the new church next Sunday.

to sharpen or refine
She needs to hone her public speaking skills.

to encourage or stir up (violent or unlawful behavior)
His speech was accused of trying to incite violence.

to praise (a person or their achievements) highly
The critics lauded the new play as a masterpiece.

to cause severe and extensive damage to
The forest fire ravaged thousands of acres of woodland.

to put right; correct
We need to rectify the error before it causes further problems.

to take the place of (someone or something previously in authority or use)
The new regulations will supersede the old ones, effective next month.

to abandon or give up
He promised never to forsake his family.

to injure severely, disfigure
The old book was so badly damaged it looked mutilated.

to obtain, especially with effort
He managed to procure the necessary documents for the visa.

to fail to resist pressure, temptation, or another negative force
He eventually succumbed to the pressure and resigned.

to put thoughts, speech, or data into written or printed form
She was asked to transcribe the interview recording.

find a way around an obstacle
They tried to circumvent the rules, but were caught.

create or bring about (an object or a situation) by deliberate use of skill and artifice
The prisoners contrived a way to escape.

praise highly; raise in rank
The choir will exalt the Lord with their voices.

charge with misconduct in office
The legislature voted to impeach the president.

to annoy, bother, or assault
The police warned people not to molest the wild animals.

to work diligently at; to travel regularly over a route
The taxi driver continued to ply his trade late into the night.

To prevent someone from accomplishing something
The police managed to thwart the robbery attempt.

be received by someone in regular or increasing amounts over time
Interest will accrue on the account daily.

To delay or prevent (someone or something) by obstructing them; hinder
The dense fog impeded their progress on the road.

sign and accept liability under (an insurance policy), thus guaranteeing payment in case of loss or damage
The bank agreed to underwrite the new venture.

to transfer or delegate (power) to a lower level
The central government decided to devolve more power to local authorities.

to cause to be loved or liked
Her kindness and humor quickly endeared her to everyone.

to be a typical example of
His dedication to his work exemplifies true professionalism.

establish (a practice or activity) as a convention or norm
The new policy aims to institutionalize fair hiring practices.

begin to grow or increase rapidly; flourish
The company's profits began to burgeon.

to clean out the bed of a harbor or river
They used a special boat to dredge the river.

to make someone feel very happy, animated, or thrilled
The roller coaster ride was exhilarating.

reject or disallow by exercising one's superior authority
The judge decided to overrule the objection.

To voluntarily give up a possession, right, or power.
He was forced to relinquish control of the company.

to imagine or contemplate
It's hard to envisage a future without technology.

Feel intense dislike or disgust for
I absolutely loathe doing laundry.

to damage the purity or integrity of; defile
He was careful not to sully his reputation.

to smear or rub with oil, typically as part of a religious ceremony
The priest will anoint the new king with holy oil.

to behave in a way that shows one considers oneself superior
Please don't condescend to me; I understand the topic perfectly.

to make something appear as if by magic
The magician promised to conjure a rabbit from his hat.

to make a doubt, feeling, or belief disappear
He tried to dispel her fears about the upcoming exam.

to evoke or draw out (a response, answer, or fact) from someone
Her questions failed to elicit any response from him.

to scatter among or between other things; to place at intervals
She interspersed her lecture with humorous anecdotes.

to go beyond the limits of
Her beauty seemed to transcend all earthly standards.

make (something) more attractive by the addition of decorative details or features
He tended to embellish the truth when telling stories.

to communicate (information or knowledge); to bestow (a quality)
The teacher tried to impart wisdom to her students.

to prevent from functioning in a normal way
The injury incapacitated him for several weeks.

reproduce or spread
Plants can propagate from cuttings.

send money or cancel a punishment
Please remit payment within 30 days.

to trouble or threaten persistently
The project was beset by delays.

to deceive or trick
He tried to dupe me into giving him money.
